source: FLEURS dev transcripts, through bournemouth_aligner's std G2P
note: Ejectives (ʼ, Georgian) and aspirated stops (ʰ, Armenian, Georgian, Korean) are tokens of their own; the burst and the puff after it belong to the stop. Korean tense consonants (ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ) have no token of their own: they are written as the plain one (k t p s t͡ɕ).

SIL.name: silence
SIL.plain: A pause: no speech. Use it for a pause the speaker makes inside a segment.

noise.name: noise
noise.plain: A non-speech sound: a breath, cough, laugh or click.

<unk>.name: unknown
<unk>.plain: The G2P wrote a sound this model has no token for. Keep its time span; the label cannot say what it is.

s.name: voiceless alveolar fricative
s.plain: s. Also used for s͈, which this model has no token of its own for

i.name: close front unrounded vowel
examples: i t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠

e.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel
e.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”

t.name: voiceless alveolar stop
t.plain: t as in “ten”. Also used for t͈, t͡ʃ`, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: ʔ a m ə t a t

k.name: voiceless velar stop
k.plain: k as in “key”. Also used for k`, k͈, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: m ɨ k ɨ n ɨ j a t

o.name: close-mid back rounded vowel
o.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”

r.name: alveolar trill
examples: p e r i v a l o n

d.name: voiced alveolar stop
examples: i t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠

ɾ.name: alveolar tap
ɾ.plain: one quick flap of the tongue, as in Spanish “pero”
examples: k ɯ ɾ i ɡ o̞

j.name: palatal approximant
examples: j ʌ ŋ ʝ j a̠ ŋ ɯ ɭ

b.name: voiced bilabial stop
examples: r ɔ m l ɛ b i t͡s

p.name: voiceless bilabial stop
examples: ʌ p s ʌ t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠
v ɔ ɾ p ɛ s

ɛ.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel
examples: qʼ v ɛ l ɑ z ɛ
d u b ɛ l v e̞

w.name: labial-velar approximant
examples: k w a̠ n ɡ w a̠ ŋ m j ʌ ŋ sʰ o̞ i m j ʌ

v.name: voiced labiodental fricative
examples: qʼ v ɛ l ɑ z ɛ
v ɾ i s k o n d e

ɡ.name: voiced velar stop
examples: k ɯ ɾ i ɡ o̞
r ɔ ɡ ɔ r t͡s

z.name: voiced alveolar fricative
examples: qʼ v ɛ l ɑ z ɛ
d z o ɾ d z

ʔ.name: glottal stop
ʔ.plain: the catch in the throat in “uh-oh”

ɔ.name: open-mid back rounded vowel
examples: s i m i n ɔ f n ɯ n

ŋ.name: velar nasal
examples: v ɔ ɾ ɔ ŋ kʰ

ʃ.name: voiceless postalveolar fricative
ʃ.plain: sh as in “ship”. Also used for t͡ʃ`, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: l ə m a ʃ a ʃ a l

ɯ.name: close back unrounded vowel
examples: i t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠

ʁ.name: voiced uvular fricative
ʁ.plain: the r of French and German

x.name: voiceless velar fricative
examples: s x v ɑ d ɑ s x v ɑ

β.name: voiced bilabial fricative
β.plain: a soft b where the lips do not close (Spanish b between vowels)
examples: ɕʰ i n β o̞ ɾ ɯ ɭ

ʒ.name: voiced postalveolar fricative
examples: ʒ ɑ m ɑ n ɑ k
ʒ i r ɑ pʰ i

ɣ.name: voiced velar fricative
ɣ.plain: a g where the tongue does not close (Dutch g, Spanish g between vowels)
examples: m e ɣ a l o
u m ɑ ɣ l ɛ s i
p a̠ ɣ ɯ m a̠ n

y.name: close front rounded vowel
y.plain: ee said with rounded lips (French “tu”, German “über”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ɨ.name: close central unrounded vowel
ɨ.plain: between ee and oo, lips spread (Polish “y”, Welsh “u”)

ɕ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative
ɕ.plain: a soft sh, with the tongue body raised (Polish “ś”)

ɲ.name: palatal nasal
examples: k ə f ɨ t ə ɲ a
k o̞ ŋ ɲ j o ŋ ɰ i

t͡s.name: voiceless alveolar affricate
examples: r ɔ ɡ ɔ r t͡s

ʏ.name: near-close front rounded vowel
ʏ.plain: i as in “sit” said with rounded lips (German “hübsch”)
examples: ʏ t̚ h a p̚ p a̠ ɡ a̠

ʎ.name: palatal lateral approximant
ʎ.plain: an l made with the tongue body, close to “ly” (Italian “gli”)
examples: pʰ i ɭ ʎ i pʰ i n

ʈ.name: voiceless retroflex stop
ʈ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”)

t͡ʃ.name: voiceless postalveolar affricate
examples: j ɨ t͡ʃ ɨ l a l u
t͡ʃ v ɛ u l ɛ b r i v

a̠.name: open front unrounded vowel, retracted
a̠.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; retracted: made a little further back in the mouth

tʰ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, aspirated
tʰ.plain: t as in “ten”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: ɡ ɑ n s ɑ kʼ u tʰ r ɛ b i tʰ

t͡ɕ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate
t͡ɕ.plain: a soft ch (Polish “ć”, Bosnian “ć”). Also used for t͡ɕ͈, which this model has no token of its own for

c.name: voiceless palatal stop
c.plain: a k made against the hard palate, close to “ty” (Hungarian “ty”, Czech “ť”)

ɭ.name: retroflex lateral approximant
ɭ.plain: l with the tongue tip curled back

ç.name: voiceless palatal fricative
ç.plain: the ch of German “ich”; like a strong h before ee
examples: ç j ʌ pʰ ø̞ ɰ i

kʰ.name: voiceless velar stop, aspirated
kʰ.plain: k as in “key”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: v ɔ ɾ ɔ ŋ kʰ
k i ɾ o̞ kʰ ɛ̝ d a̠

ʌ.name: open-mid back unrounded vowel
ʌ.plain: u as in “cup”. Also used for ʌ̹, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: ʌ p s ʌ t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠

sʰ.name: voiceless alveolar fricative, aspirated
sʰ.plain: s; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

pʰ.name: voiceless bilabial stop, aspirated
pʰ.plain: p as in “pen”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: pʰ i ɭ ʎ i pʰ i n

k̚.name: voiceless velar stop, unreleased
k̚.plain: k as in “key”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently
examples: k w a̠ ɦ a̠ k̚ t͡ɕ ʌ k̚

o̞.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, lowered
o̞.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; lowered: a little more open; a lowered fricative is a smooth approximant with no friction
examples: k ɯ ɾ i ɡ o̞

ɟ.name: voiced palatal stop
ɟ.plain: a g made against the hard palate, close to “dy” (Hungarian “gy”, Czech “ď”)
examples: ɣ a ŋ ɟ e t i c i

ɸ.name: voiceless bilabial fricative
ɸ.plain: blowing through nearly closed lips. Also used for ɸʷ, which this model has no token of its own for

d͡z.name: voiced alveolar affricate
examples: ʃ ɛ i d͡z l ɛ b ɑ

ɦ.name: voiced glottal fricative
ɦ.plain: a breathy, voiced h (Dutch and Czech h)

ʝ.name: voiced palatal fricative
examples: j ʌ ŋ ʝ j a̠ ŋ ɯ ɭ

i̯.name: close front unrounded vowel, non-syllabic
i̯.plain: ee as in “see”; non-syllabic: the weak, glide-like half of a diphthong; it is not a syllable on its own
examples: ð i̯ a θ e t i

ɕʰ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative, aspirated
ɕʰ.plain: a soft sh, with the tongue body raised (Polish “ś”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: k ʌ ɕʰ i d a̠

ɛ̝.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel, raised
ɛ̝.plain: e as in “bed”; raised: a little closer (tongue higher) than the plain symbol
examples: t ɛ̝ m u n e̞

t͡ɕʰ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate, aspirated
t͡ɕʰ.plain: a soft ch (Polish “ć”, Bosnian “ć”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ǎ.name: open front unrounded vowel, accent ˇ (rising)
ǎ.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; accent ˇ (rising): the G2P's dictionary marks a rising pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t̚.name: voiceless alveolar stop, unreleased
t̚.plain: t as in “ten”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently
examples: i t̚ s ɯ m n i d a̠

e̞.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, lowered
e̞.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; lowered: a little more open; a lowered fricative is a smooth approximant with no friction

u̯.name: close back rounded vowel, non-syllabic
u̯.plain: oo as in “food”; non-syllabic: the weak, glide-like half of a diphthong; it is not a syllable on its own. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ǒ.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, accent ˇ (rising)
ǒ.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; accent ˇ (rising): the G2P's dictionary marks a rising pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ě.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, accent ˇ (rising)
ě.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; accent ˇ (rising): the G2P's dictionary marks a rising pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

r̥.name: alveolar trill, voiceless
r̥.plain: a rolled r; voiceless: said without vocal-fold vibration, as if whispered. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ǐ.name: close front unrounded vowel, accent ˇ (rising)
ǐ.plain: ee as in “see”; accent ˇ (rising): the G2P's dictionary marks a rising pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

χ.name: voiceless uvular fricative
χ.plain: a rougher ch made at the uvula (Welsh “ch”)

p̚.name: voiceless bilabial stop, unreleased
p̚.plain: p as in “pen”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently

ê.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, accent ˆ (falling)
ê.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; accent ˆ (falling): the G2P's dictionary marks a falling pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t͡sʰ.name: voiceless alveolar affricate, aspirated
t͡sʰ.plain: ts as in “cats”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

á.name: open front unrounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
á.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

é.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
é.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ó.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
ó.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

í.name: close front unrounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
í.plain: ee as in “see”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

tʼ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, ejective
tʼ.plain: t as in “ten”; ejective: a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs
examples: ʃ tʼ ɑ tʼ ɛ b s

ô.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, accent ˆ (falling)
ô.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; accent ˆ (falling): the G2P's dictionary marks a falling pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

kʼ.name: voiceless velar stop, ejective
kʼ.plain: k as in “key”; ejective: a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs

t͡ʃʰ.name: voiceless postalveolar affricate, aspirated
t͡ʃʰ.plain: ch as in “church”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ø̞.name: close-mid front rounded vowel, lowered
ø̞.plain: e said with rounded lips (German “schön”, French “peu”); lowered: a little more open; a lowered fricative is a smooth approximant with no friction

pʼ.name: voiceless bilabial stop, ejective
pʼ.plain: p as in “pen”; ejective: a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs
examples: pʼ ɔ pʼ u l ɑ r u l i

ɰ.name: velar approximant
ɰ.plain: a g so weak the tongue never closes
examples: k o̞ ŋ ɲ j o ŋ ɰ i

ʍ.name: voiceless labial-velar approximant
ʍ.plain: a breathy w (“wh” in some accents). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t͡sʼ.name: voiceless alveolar affricate, ejective
t͡sʼ.plain: ts as in “cats”; ejective: a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs

ɱ.name: labiodental nasal
ɱ.plain: m made with the lower lip against the teeth, before f or v (“comfort”)
examples: s i ɱ f o n a

qʼ.name: voiceless uvular stop, ejective
qʼ.plain: a k made further back, at the uvula (Uzbek “q”); ejective: a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs

t͡ʃʼ.name: ejective postalveolar affricate
t͡ʃʼ.plain: ch said with a pop from the throat, no breath
examples: ɑ ɣ t͡ʃʼ u r v i l ɔ b i tʰ

ɛ̂.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel, accent ˆ (falling)
ɛ̂.plain: e as in “bed”; accent ˆ (falling): the G2P's dictionary marks a falling pitch accent. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language
